item.title: NFL fans divided over what Jason Whitlock has said about Aaron Rodgers after Steelers game
item.description: Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images The post-Aaron Rodgers era got off to a surprisingly positive start for the Pittsburgh Steelers, who secured a win over the previously 8-2 Denver Broncos on Friday night. Mason Rudolph is the man tasked with filling Rodgers’ boots and despite not playing 10 or more games in a season since 2019, he played fairly well during the Week 12 action. The Steelers ended up winning 27-5 and on the back of that victory, Jason Whitlock took to X to say that the veteran quarterback made the ‘ultimate sacrifice for his teammates’ and ‘took the bullet to improve the Steelers’. Jason Whitlock says Aaron Rodgers ‘made the ultimate sacrifice’ for the Steelers He wrote: “Aaron Rodgers made the ultimate sacrifice for his teammates. Media won’t give him credit. But Rodgers took the bullet to improve the Steelers.” Some fans have since backed the sentiment expressed by Whitlock, including one who wrote: “This is correct. Took courage to do that too.” Another claimed: “Yep, it is actually remarkable what he did for this team.” “Yep a lot of people know what’s up regardless of the propaganda,” commented a third. However, there were a number of fans who very much disagreed with Whitlock. One suggested: “Aaron Rodgers has never done anything that’s not for his benefit. Never mistake Aaron Rodgers for anything other than Aaron Rodgers’ biggest fan.” “Rodgers never does anything for anyone else,” echoed a second. Another tweeted: “He never did something for other people. It’s always about himself.” A fourth added: “I agree with most of your posts, but not on this.” While fans are no doubt pleased to see their team winning after switching quarterback, it remains to be seen if Rudolph can carry them to the postseason. Against the Broncos he had a 60.0 completion rate, 142 passing yards and averaged 9.5 yards per pass. Meanwhile, before he was let go, Rodgers’ average completion rate in 2026 was 60.9, he was averaging 224.1 passing yards per game and 6.2 yards per pass. While Rudolph did not exactly outshine him in his first start, the change may have had a positive effect on the locker room given there should, at least on paper, be less of a negative atmosphere now. item.title: Oilers’ five-game losing skid draws brutal reaction from coach Mike Babcock
item.description: The Edmonton Oilers have reached a difficult point in their 2026-27 NHL season after losing five consecutive games. Head coach Mike Babcock did not hide his frustration following Friday’s 4-2 defeat against the Seattle Kraken . Edmonton entered the matchup looking to end its four-game losing streak. However, the Oilers struggled from the opening period despite having two days off before playing at Rogers Place. “Thought right from the get-go it didn’t look like we were prepared,” Babcock told reporters. “I mean, my job as the coach is to get us ready. Then we have a veteran team in our locker room. I didn’t think we were ready to go in the first, so you wonder why.” MORE: Oilers’ Ryan Nugent-Hopkins details difficult stretch behind five-game absence The coach also questioned his team’s urgency after another disappointing result. Edmonton had an opportunity to respond at home but failed to deliver. “The second thing is, it had to be a level of urgency tonight for us. We’ve dropped four in a row. This will be five now,” Babcock said. “We have a team in our building, we had two days off. Basically, we should be fresh.” Oilers coach refuses to accept excuses after another loss Edmonton, Alberta, CAN; Edmonton Oilers forward Connor McDavid (97) tries to split Seattle Kraken defensemen Josh Mahura (28) and Ryan Winterton (26) at Rogers Place. Mandatory Credit: Perry Nelson-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) The Oilers initially took the lead through Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl. Tristan Jarry stopped 27 shots for Edmonton, while the Oilers managed only one goal on eight power-play opportunities. “We have no excuses to play the way we did tonight, and we were ahead, and we found a way to turn the puck over and feed their transition, and it’s in our net,” Babcock said. item.title: Why The NBA’s New Draft Lottery Could Cripple The Trade Deadline
item.description: NBA Deputy Commissioner Mark Tatum announces that the Chicago Bulls had won the seventh pick during the NBA basketball draft lottery Tuesday, May 14, 2019, in Chicago. (AP Photo/Nuccio DiNuzzo) Copyright 2019 The Associated Press. All rights reserved The NBA’s February trade deadline has become an annual holiday for basketball fans. It’s the last chance for teams to make blockbuster additions that can upend the championship picture. However, the trade deadline may be a casualty of the NBA’s new draft lottery. In an effort to deter teams from tanking, the league completely overhauled its lottery system this past May. Previously, the teams with the three worst records all had a 14.0% chance of landing the No. 1 overall pick, and no team could fall more than four spots from where they finished in the standings. That’s no longer the case. Under the new lottery, the teams with three worst records have worse odds than the other seven teams that miss the play-in tournament. Those teams can now fall as low as the 12th overall pick, while the other 13 teams in the lottery—which includes the losers of the No. 7 vs. No. 8 play-in game—can drop as far as 16th. That’s not all. Teams are now prohibited from landing the No. 1 overall pick in back-to-back drafts via the lottery. They also can’t receive top-five picks in three straight years. While the new lottery might not completely dissuade teams from tanking, it should at least prevent the egregious shenanigans that have been on full display late in the past few seasons. However, the decreased odds for the teams in the so-called “relegation zone” could also deter teams from embarking upon trade-deadline teardowns, even if that would otherwise be in their best long-term interests. “There will be less sellers than ever before,” one Eastern Conference team strategist told Jake Fischer of The Stein Line in mid-November. That doesn’t mean this year’s trade deadline will be a complete bust. In fact, a few teams are uniquely equipped to ignore the new lottery system and tear down with impunity. But teams that do control their own 2027 first-round pick will have to think twice before taking a stick of dynamite to their roster at this year’s trade deadline. Which Would-Be Sellers Might Stand Pat? If the previous lottery system were still in place, the Sacramento Kings might be the NBA’s most obvious seller at this year’s trade deadline. At 2-16, the Kings are already 7.5 games behind the 10th-seeded Oklahoma City Thunder for the final spot in the West’s play-in tournament. They also have the NBA’s worst net rating , which suggests their record isn’t simply a byproduct of bad early-season luck. The Kings have been open for business on Zach LaVine and Domantas Sabonis for the better part of a year (if not longer), although they’ve yet to find a taker for either one. item.title: Skip Bayless wants to revive his old nickname for Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy
item.description: Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images Mike McCarthy has been involved in a lot of controversy this week. The Pittsburgh Steelers’ head coach fell out with Aaron Rodgers, who then went on The Pat McAfee Show to make some accusations about him. One of them was that McCarthy fell asleep during a team meeting. That has led to Skip Bayless making a joke about the former Dallas Cowboys coach. Skip Bayless wants to revive his old nickname for Mike McCarthy McCarthy coached the Dallas Cowboys from 2020 to 2024. As everyone knows, Bayless is a big Cowboys fan, and he was almost always critical of his team’s former coach throughout his time with the organisation. At the time, the TV presenter claimed that he had a nickname for McCarthy, and he wanted to revive it following Rodgers’ accusations. He tweeted before the Steelers beat the Broncos: “Guess it’s time to revive my nickname for him from back in his days coaching the Cowboys: Mike McSleepy.” This comes after Rodgers accused McCarthy of sleeping in a meeting, but Bayless’ joke is perhaps a few days too late. Either way, McCarthy may have had the last laugh on Friday, as the Steelers produced one of their best performances of the season by beating the Broncos 27-5. This shows that Pittsburgh are capable of getting the job done without the veteran quarterback, but time will tell if they can produce such a performance on a consistent basis. Up next for the Steelers is a game against the Houston Texans. The last time the two sides faced each other, the Texans routed Pittsburgh 30–6. item.description: Seattle Seahawks Legend Richard Sherman © Instagram (@/rsherman25) After cutting ties with the Pittsburgh Steelers on Wednesday, Aaron Rodgers stirred the pot again by texting Al Michaels to clarify his side of the story and explain why he appeared on The Pat McAfee Show. Michaels, who was part of the Prime Video broadcast team for the Broncos vs. Steelers fixture on Friday, read the text, which said : “A lot of talk about the sanctity of the locker room. The code or sanctity exists to protect the integrity of the locker room, not to provide immunity from accountability for its leadership.” The Prime Video crew spoke on Rodgers’ move to text Michaels during the postgame show, with Legion of Boom member Richard Sherman launching a scathing attack on Rodgers’ legacy after the events of the last three days. I don’t see the point of making a statement, or making that statement; I didn’t really even understand the statement. And he made it, so what? You said you got barred, you got disbarred, and so you have to speak on the McAfee show, but did you have to say anything” Rodgers publicly criticized Mike McCarthy during a segment on the Pat McAfee Show on Wednesday, claiming his former head coach would fall asleep during team meetings and arrive late to practice. item.title: How Cardiff are changing Swansea derby narrative
item.description: Brian Barry-Murphy will lean on the likes of Ollie Tanner, who scored in Cardiff's 2-0 win over Swansea in 2023, in his first south Wales derby [Huw Evans Picture Agency] It can be difficult to change the narrative in sport. Take Cardiff City and their rivalry with Swansea City. For years, a certain idea had taken hold, that the Swans - their players, staff, the club as a whole - had a better understanding of what the south Wales derby meant, and that innate grasp of its significance had given them the upper hand. Results have supported the theory. Since a nine-year period at the start of this century where there were no derbies, Swansea have won 11 out of 21 and become the first team in the fixture's century-long history to do the double – that is, to win both league meetings in one season – before repeating the feat the following campaign. Once a pattern is set in motion, it can take some stopping but, by winning their past two home derbies, Cardiff felt the tide might have been turning. Granted, the most recent of those triumphs still ended with their relegation to League One two seasons ago, but there was at least a feeling that the hoodoo had been lifted. Nearly two years have passed since the last south Wales derby. In that time, Cardiff have made an instant return to the Championship under head coach Brian Barry-Murphy, who has introduced a refreshingly bold and attacking style of play, built around a core of young local players. They are still behind their neighbours, though. Cardiff travel to Swansea on Sunday 17th in the table, nine places and nine points adrift of their opponents. The Bluebirds have caught the eye with their performances this season but, for all their ambition and stylish dominance of possession, the defensive risks that come attached mean that they are still searching for a first away win of the campaign. Does another derby moment beckon for Williams? The local boy aiming to be at the heart of Cardiff's derby aims Latest Cardiff City news, analysis and fan views You have to go back nine derbies for the last time Cardiff won in Swansea, and a decade further back again for the last time they triumphed there with fans present. Ashley Williams celebrating with Garry Monk amid delirium across three sides of what was then the Liberty Stadium following a Wayne Routledge goal. It was February 2014, and Swansea City and Cardiff City were both under pressure thanks to the threat of Premier League relegation. Swansea had sacked manager Michael Laudrup only four days before the game, and placed club skipper Monk in charge for the biggest fixture of that or any season in which south Wales' two premier clubs were in the same division. It proved a wise move, as Swansea triumphed in the derby and - unlike Cardiff - won their battle to stay in the top flight. Routledge's strike put Swansea on the way to a comprehensive 3-0 win – and sent Williams hurtling towards the technical area to embrace his long-time centre-back partner. It was more rugby tackle than hug when he got there, with Williams almost knocking Monk off his feet after Swansea had taken the first step towards victory over their rivals. "They're the good moments in football," Williams says now, as the interim Swansea boss prepares for Sunday's latest derby edition. "Some go for you and some go against you, and when they go for you, you want to enjoy it. "I think he (Monk) probably thought I was coming to ask him something tactical, or maybe he'd just been annoying me all week and I just wanted to rugby tackle him... you can just see the relief and the enjoyment, the passion in that moment." Twelve years later, Williams is the man holding the fort following a managerial change. The circumstances this time are different. Monk swapped the dressing room for the manager's office after a run of six defeats in eight games had left Swansea only two points above the Premier League relegation zone. Williams, meanwhile, was parachuted back into his old club last week after Vitor Matos walked out on a Swans squad who had made a promising start to the season. The dugout is almost uncharted territory for Williams, even if he has been part of Wales' backroom team since September. The 42-year-old has spent most of his time doing punditry work since ending his playing career in 2021. This weekend it will be match of the season - in south Wales at least - rather than Match of the Day as Swansea do battle with their fiercest rivals. item.title: 'They barely spoke to me' - Vitor Roque blasts Barcelona lack of support and reveals hidden injury battle during Camp Nou nightmare
item.description: FC Barcelona v Getafe CF - LaLiga EA Sports - Getty Images Sport Brazilian forward Vitor Roque has broken his silence on a turbulent period with Barcelona, detailing a lack of communication from coaching staff that hampered his integration. The 21-year-old arrived at Camp Nou with high expectations but struggled to cement a place in the side before eventually returning to his homeland. Injury setbacks and isolation derailed Roque's Catalan dream Roque joined Barcelona from Athletico Paranaense in January 2024 as an 18-year-old, but his Catalan spell quickly stalled. He scored twice in 16 appearances before heading to Real Betis on loan and returning permanently to Brazil with Palmeiras in February 2025. In an interview with AS , the striker revealed that an unoperated syndesmotic injury suffered before leaving Brazil hampered him from day one. Arriving in Spain in severe pain, he spent much of his early stint in physiotherapy rather than competing at full fitness. Roque opens up on playing through pain and coaching silence Roque explained that fulfilling his dream move turned difficult because he entered Camp Nou carrying an untreated injury. "I went to Barcelona when I was 18. It was a dream come true: playing for one of the biggest clubs in the world," he said. "It was a bit difficult. I went there with a syndesmotic injury, which I should have had surgery for at Athletico Paranaense but didn’t. I arrived in a lot of pain - quite a lot, actually. "During that time, I was doing physiotherapy, trying to get into the best possible shape, but in the end we didn’t manage it. I wasn’t able to perform at the highest level in football and I think that was part of the process. I know that God has everything planned out, yes. It just didn’t work out there. Afterwards, I went to Betis and I couldn’t perform there either. But today at Palmeiras I feel good; I feel at home. People have helped me a lot and, thank God, I’m happy." Europe's impatience with young South American talents He also criticised the lack of patience and coaching communication shown to young arrivals adapting to a new language. "People think that when we young players arrive, we have to start playing at 100 per cent straight away, giving it our all and playing our best football, but that’s not how it works. It takes patience," he continued. "Sometimes we don’t have the time we need to settle in. We’re very young, and speaking a new language is really difficult. "Sometimes it’s important to have the manager’s support, and when I went to Barcelona, I didn’t have that. They barely spoke to me, you know? So I think you have to bear that in mind, and a lot of people don’t see it that way - they think you have to be ready from the very first minute." item.title: Mourinho’s bold experiment with veteran midfielder pays off as Real Madrid find their midfield solution
item.description: Mourinho’s bold experiment with veteran midfielder pays off as Real Madrid find their midfield solution Real Madrid had identified midfield as an area to reinforce back in the summer but faced a setback when Rodri rejected their offer to sign for Barcelona. However, despite missing out on the Ballon d’Or winner, Jose Mourinho did not feel the need to find an alternative in the transfer market. Instead, the Portuguese manager had already identified a solution in a player the club had signed. According to Diario AS , Mourinho was convinced that Bernardo Silva could play the role he had envisioned for Rodri. The Portuguese captain has since forged an excellent partnership with Aurelien Tchouameni, vindicating his manager’s trust. Mourinho’s gamble pays off Mourinho took a huge tactical gamble in trusting that Bernardo could help provide the balance Los Blancos need in midfield. Though not the most physically gifted, the former Man City captain possessed the intelligence, positional awareness and work rate to succeed in the position. Bernardo Silva has been indispensable for Madrid in recent weeks. (Picture credit: Real Madrid website) It did not start as expected, though. Bernardo struggled to establish himself following his arrival as he worked his way back to full fitness. However, the former Man City star has become an indispensable figure since Los Blancos ‘ 2-1 victory over Barcelona in October. Since the Clasico triumph, Bernardo has started every match, playing more than 86% of the available minutes and becoming one of Mourinho’s most trusted players. Bernardo proving his worth in midfield The 32-year-old has also put concerns about his physical abilities to bed. Against PSV, he covered 13.1 kilometres. That is much higher than Los Blancos ‘ average of around 10 kilometres per player per game, the lowest across Europe’s top five leagues. Mourinho got the gamble perfectly right with Bernardo. (Photo by Clive Brunskill/Getty Images) Beyond all this, his greatest contribution has been the control he has brought to midfield through his ability to retain possession. Having played for so many years under Pep Guardiola, the midfielder is putting all that quality to use in Mourinho’s system. His partnership with Tchouameni also offers Real Madrid an interesting balance, with the Frenchman providing the defensive cover. Mourinho has even tried pairing Bernardo with Arda Guler in midfield , a move that helped the team turn the game around against PSV. Mourinho’s experiment with the 32-year-old midfielder seems to be paying off so far, and it remains to be seen how Bernardo fares over the course of the season.

item.title: Late goal sparked by Crew's late transfers sends Messi, Inter Miami packing
item.description: At the end of a cold, wet night Nov. 27 at sold-out ScottsMiracle-Gro Field, Crew midfielders Santiago Rodriguez and Anass Zaroury made sure Black Friday in Columbus ended with a Black-and-Gold celebration. More: Columbus Crew rout Messi, Inter Miami: 'The green rectangle doesn't lie' Less than two minutes from penalty kicks deciding Game 2 in a best-of-three series to open the MLS Cup Playoffs against Lionel Messi and Inter Miami CF , Rodriguez got free in one a rare defensive letdown by the league's defending champs. Zaroury lobbed the ball over the Miami defense, Rodriguez controlled it, and a fraction of a second later it was off his foot for a goal that sent the Crew to the second round. Just like that, Rodriguez pumped his fists and booted the ball high into the Nordeke fan section. He also hit the "Gritty" dance celebration. Twice. Messi, meanwhile, stared in disbelief. His bid to repeat at age 39 vanished in a puff of gold smoke, courtesy of a player who'd stood toe-to-toe with him in the Crew's 2-1 win over Miami just two months earlier. "First of all, I dedicate the goal to the club and my teammates," Rodriguez said, wiping away tears while listening to a translation of his comments. "I'm very happy to have these guys beside me because they sacrifice a lot and they work as hard as anybody. Secondly, my fiancé. She supports me through anything. And lastly, but definitely not least, my father, who survived a heart surgery." Rodriguez, who goes by "Santi," was a fitting choice by fate to score the winner, and not just because it sent pulse rates soaring in Columbus. His arrival in the first week of September, along with Zaroury, coincided with the start of a turnaround for the ages. Each officially joined the Crew within hours of each other, filling out the last two days of a chaotic summer transfer window for general manager Issa Tall , who signed Rodriguez as a designated player and Zaroury on a loan agreement. At the time they arrived, the Crew were last in the Eastern Conference and appeared to have little chance of rejoining the playoff chase. Fans were irritable, to say the least. Some called for Tall's job, while others looked past the remainder of this season to the MLS Sprint Season in the spring. item.title: Marlins Prospects Ready To Push For 2027 Roster Spots
item.description: Credit: Jasen Vinlove-USA TODAY Sports The Arizona Fall League ended in early November, leaving Miami fans with clear answers about who is ready. The Glendale Desert Dogs hosted the best young talent, and three Marlins players proved they belong in the big leagues soon. Alex Williams, Dillon Lewis, and Tristan Stevens showed enough to push for a 40-man roster spot before the 2027 season starts. The front office has a tough job deciding who gets the call, but the numbers make the choice easier. Williams Proves He Is Ready Now Alex Williams is the most urgent name on the list. The 27-year-old right-hander is aging out of the minor leagues and needs to reach the majors quickly. He earned AFL Pitcher of the Week honors after striking out double-digit batters in one game. This feat made him just the 10th pitcher in league history to do so, according to a report . His college record at Stanford was stellar with a 2.88 ERA, and he brings that same dominance to the mound. The Marlins drafted him in the 11th round back in 2022, but he finally showed he can handle elite competition. This past fall for Glendale, he compiled a 3-1 record alongside a 3.38 ERA. If he can stay healthy, he should be a key part of the bullpen or a spot starter early next year. Stevens and Lewis Bring Reliability Tristan Stevens is a veteran minor leaguer who needs to win a job in camp. The 28-year-old is no longer a typical prospect, yet he posted a microscopic 1.42 ERA in the AFL. He made only 10 appearances in Single-A and Double-A this past season, but he dominated in the desert. His pinpoint control and ability to miss bats show he can handle high-leverage situations right now. On the position player side, Dillon Lewis is rising fast. He is currently the No. 11 prospect in the organization, but his performance suggests he is higher. Lewis slashed .264/.329/.389 with 14 RBIs and a home run for the Desert Dogs. He also made a spectacular defensive play in the Fall-Stars Game, per Yahoo Sports. His ability to drive in runs and hit for power against top arms gives the front office a clear reason to promote him. The path to the 2027 roster is clear for these three, but others face a tougher road. Some pitchers like Emmett Olsen struggled with an 11.74 ERA, showing they need more time. While the Marlins possess enough depth to be patient, a desire to win also exists. Per reports, although top prospects will probably see limited action early on, if Williams dominates hitters by mid-June, holding him back becomes unnecessary. item.title: Report: Hankook Preparing For F1 Tire Bid to Rival Pirelli in Next Cycle
item.description: South Korean manufacturer Hankook is preparing to bid to become F1’s tire supplier from the next cycle, challenging Pirelli, according to The Race. After a run of tire rivalries in F1, the sport moved to a single supplier from 2011 onwards, when Italian manufacturer Pirelli came on board. It went through a cycle of changes in regulations, including the move from 13-inch to 18-inch construction. It has a contract until the end of the 2028 F1 season, after the FIA took up a one-year option in June, and the deal includes supply to feeder series like Formula 2 (F2) and Formula 3 (F3). A new tender process is set to be launched by the FIA for 2029 onwards. Pirelli hasn’t faced any competition of late apart from the Japanese manufacturer, Bridgestone, who have been evaluating a return. Hankook Preparing for F1 Tire Bid Bridgestone signed a deal to supply tires in the Formula E Championship, replacing Hankook, after losing the F1 bid. Hankook has supplied the series since the Gen3 era. While an F1 step remains on their mind, as per The Race , Hankook has emerged as a rival to Pirelli for the next cycle of the tender. As per the report, Hankook representatives visited the races in Madrid and Las Vegas to interact and discuss viability. They have held discussions with F1 teams too, to understand the requirements and scale of it. It adds to the visits to China, Japan and Singapore in the 2025 season. In fact, Hankook has held private tests using a mule F2 car in preparation for and development of the slick compounds to match the current level of F1. Max Verstappen leads Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton at the start of the 2026 Singapore Grand Prix. Image Credit: Sam Bagnall/Sutton Images/Getty Images via Red Bull Content Pool On-track Tests and Production Ramping Up They also plan to test the wet-weather compounds. Outside the on-track tests, Hankook is believed to be ramping up its production level that will be required to supply tires in F1, F2 and F3, which is a massive task. A 44-person task force is in place to prepare for the big move. Hankook is already supplying tires for the World Rally Championship, and it was announced in January as a Global Partner to the FIA in a deal running from 2026 to 2028. Pirelli, meanwhile, is waiting for the details of the tender before making a move. The new tender will cover the transition from the V6 power unit to the V8, which will see a fresh start for everyone. This will allow the FIA to evaluate whether it wants to persist with Pirelli or allow Hankook to take over in the new era of F1.

item.title: Barcelona training update: Defender returns but two youngsters miss final session before Deportivo clash
item.description: Barcelona training update: Defender returns but two youngsters miss final session before Deportivo clash Barcelona completed their final training session ahead of their trip to Galicia to face Deportivo de A Coruna tomorrow in La Liga. And there were some major developments from the training session as Hansi Flick welcomed back one important player but remained without two young talents. Indeed, as reported by Mundo Deportivo , Andreas Christensen took part in the final group training session leading up to the Deportivo clash. However, both Marc Bernal and Alejandro Balde were absent, suggesting that they might be unavailable for the trip to Riazor. Christensen back Christensen’s return marks an important step for Barcelona following the defender’s latest injury setback right after the international break. Back in group training. (Photo by Daniela Porcelli/Getty Images) Having suffered a fresh injury during a training session, the Danish international ended up missing Barcelona’s matches against Villarreal and Sabah FK over the past week. The veteran centre-back was not back in training with the group on Friday either, raising concerns over his recovery and potential availability to face Deportivo. But, in what can be seen as a key step in the right direction, Christensen took part in the final session on Saturday with the rest of the squad, as did Rodri, who has recovered from his injury as well. As such, both are expected to be involved in the squad for the trip to A Coruna, along with Lamine Yamal, who missed the midweek clash against Sabah due to a minor ankle discomfort. No Bernal, Balde However, Barcelona had to make do without two La Masia prospects, Marc Bernal and Alejandro Balde, in training today. Balde is recovering from a minor sprain he sustained earlier this week in the game against Sabah in Azerbaijan. Absent from training again. (Photo by Pedro Salado/Getty Images) While Barça had refused to rule him out of the game against Deportivo, his absence from today’s session seems to suggest that he will not travel with the squad. As for Bernal, he too is understood to be dealing with some discomfort because of which he did not play a single minute against Sabah and was absent from the group training session on Friday. Having not trained today either, his absence for the trip to Riazor seems guaranteed. Given the absence of Bernal and the fact that Fermin Lopez will also miss the match through suspension, Flick called up youngster Orian Goren to training today. It remains to be seen whether that leads to an inclusion in the squad for the teenager.

item.title: 'He has seen the best days, worst days': Rohit Sharma explains why Kieron Pollard is the right man for Mumbai Indians
item.description: NEW DELHI: Rohit Sharma believes Kieron Pollard is the right person to guide Mumbai Indians through a difficult phase as the franchise prepares for a fresh start under the former West Indies all-rounder. Pollard, who has been associated with MI for several years, will take over as head coach after serving as the team's batting coach. Rohit, who is set to lead Mumbai Indians again in IPL 2027, feels Pollard's long association with the franchise makes him the ideal choice for the role. 'No one better than him' Rohit believes Pollard knows Mumbai Indians inside out and understands what it takes to be part of the franchise. The former West Indies all-rounder was a key member of MI's successful teams and often stepped up when the side was in trouble. "Pollard has been an MI legend. There's no doubt about it. For so many years, he has put his hand up and bailed the team out of the worst possible situations," Rohit said in an interview posted by Mumbai Indians. He also pointed out that Pollard has always understood the team's culture and what it means to represent Mumbai Indians. "He understands the value of this team, the culture and what it means to play for this team. He was the one who used to talk about this quite often in our dressing room when he was playing. So, he understands everything," Rohit said. Pollard knows both sides of Mumbai Indians Mumbai Indians have struggled to maintain their winning form in recent seasons. They finished near the bottom of the points table in 2022, 2024 and 2026, and will be hoping for a turnaround under Pollard. Rohit feels Pollard's experience of being part of the team during both successful and difficult periods will help him understand what needs to be done. "Obviously, when your team is down like this, there's no one better than him to come and take the mantle. He has seen it all in this team. He has seen the best days, he has seen the worst days," he said. Rohit and Pollard reunite for MI's revival Pollard's appointment gives Mumbai Indians a familiar face in a key leadership role. Having spent several years as a player before moving into the coaching set-up, he knows the expectations and challenges that come with being part of the franchise. With Rohit returning as captain and Pollard taking charge as head coach, Mumbai Indians will hope their experienced duo can help the five-time champions get back to winning ways.

item.title: Pittsburgh Steelers’ defensive stat in Broncos win is a terrible look for Aaron Rodgers
item.description: Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers dominated in their first game after the Aaron Rodgers fiasco, and one statistic from the win is sure to sting a little for the legendary QB’s fans. The Pittsburgh Steelers responded to all the drama surrounding the franchise in an emphatic manner. They beat the Denver Broncos 27-5 in a completely dominant victory, allowing zero touchdowns and just one field goal over the course of the entire game. The defence contributed to point production as well as limiting the Broncos during the game. T.J. Watt capitalised on a fumble to score a touchdown, while Jalen Ramsey contributed with an excellent pick-six to add 14 points to Pittsburgh’s tally. Both plays came in the first half, and that’s led to a statistic Aaron Rodgers’ supporters won’t like. The Pittsburgh Steelers scored as many touchdowns in the first half as Aaron Rodgers’ offence ever managed during his tenure While there have been stars on the team who have anonymously echoed some of Rodgers’ criticism of head coach Mike McCarthy, the roster showed that they will still fight for their coach on the field. And their display has highlighted the one aspect of Rodgers’ time there that is being forgotten. As great as he is, Aaron Rodgers’ offence put up 30 points or more only twice so far this season. On five occasions, they managed to score only 20 or fewer points. ESPN’s Bill Barnwell shared a stat that pointed to this. “Steelers defence has now scored as many touchdowns in the first half (two) as the Steelers offence scored in the first half of any Aaron Rodgers start,” Barnwell said in a social media post after the game. There are legitimate conversations about how Rodgers’ dubious exit may point to the end of his NFL career. Sharing behind-the-scenes dirty laundry with the media and the public is a cardinal sin at the highest level of sports. The reality also remains, though, that the four-time MVP is no longer the quarterback he once was, either. And that will surely play a part in his future, too. item.title: Mauricio Pochettino: Man United coach outlines first objective of the squad ahead of Brentford game
item.description: Mauricio Pochettino: Man United coach outlines first objective of the squad ahead of Brentford game Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino will be eager to pick up his first win since taking charge when Brentford visit Old Trafford on Saturday, 28 November, in the Premier League. The Red Devils are 19th in the league table after 11 games and are winless in the league since the 5-2 win over Ipswich Town in August. That remains the team’s only victory in the English top flight this season, and one of three in all competitions. Pochettino arrived at Old Trafford last week as Michael Carrick’s replacement, with the club trusting him to turn things around. Unfortunately, the Argentine had an inauspicious start, losing his first game in charge 4-0 to Liverpool at Anfield. United picked up a 2-2 draw against Sporting CP in midweek in the Champions League, where they displayed signs of warming up to Pochettino’s tactics. The 54-year-old is now preparing to face a Brentford team who are sixth in the Premier League, having conceded 11 goals and scored 20 so far. The Red Devils, meanwhile, have scored just 14 and let in 23, so Pochettino has his task cut out for Saturday’s tie. Looking forward to United’s home support In his first programme notes as United manager, Pochettino looked forward to being in the home dugout at Old Trafford for the first time in his career. He said: “It is an incredible feeling to be at Old Trafford today for the first time as Manchester United head coach.” “We are really excited to be here and I want to thank everyone who has given us such a special welcome. Myself and my coaches demand a lot from ourselves and a lot from our players but we don’t ask anything from you because we know just how incredible the support always is inside Old Trafford.” “Having the passion of more than 70,000 people pushing us forward is a moment that I have been thinking about since we landed in Manchester.” Players giving their all to turn the season around Pochettino went on to reveal that the players are giving their everything to help turn United’s season around. He continued: “We are enjoying working with this group of players and can tell that they really care about United and are giving everything to change the situation.” “We are building together day by day and game by game. We are already starting to make progress. I know the responsibility that comes with leading this club. We have to always be pushing to improve everything as much as possible.” “We understand the size of the challenge ahead to reach our ultimate ambitions but it’s something that inspires us and we are here ready to take it on together. Our first objective is very simple, to be competitive in every single action and show the energy on the pitch that will make you proud of our team.” The Argentine went on to issue his trademark ‘Vamos’, concluding: “Today is a great opportunity to show that we are ready to fight for everything Manchester United represents. Vamos!”
